title: Implement Regular Expression Pattern Modifiers proposal
body: This is likely a good first bug for someone getting started on contributing to SpiderMonkey. The implementation is already contained in the upstream irregexp library and controlled by a JIT option. What's left is to add a preference that controls the feature, following the linked example, move `regexp-modifiers` in `js/src/tests/test262-update.py` to `FEATURE_CHECK_NEEDED`, and re-import the tests according to the SpiderMonkey test instructions.

symptoms_visible: The upstream regexp-modifier implementation exists, but SpiderMonkey still needs a preference for it and its passing test262 tests need to be enabled and re-imported.
N0.label: N0 implementation work requested

symptoms_visible: I have one patch adding the preference and another patch adding the regexp-modifier tests.
N1.label: N1 initial patches authored

symptoms_visible: The patched tests pass when run locally, but the autoland SpiderMonkey jobs report regexp-modifier test failures.
N2.label: N2 local and CI results differ

symptoms_visible: After adding the known local failures to the skip list, the combined landing still produced regexp-modifier failures in SpiderMonkey CI and was backed out.
N2_x.label: N2_x skip-list attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The CI log reports `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier` for enabled regexp-modifier tests, including a pattern such as `(?m:es.$)`.
N3.label: N3 exact CI failure collected

symptoms_visible: The preference patch is now present, while enabling the full test set still exposes the repeated-flag syntax errors.
N4.label: N4 preference landed separately

symptoms_visible: With `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` enabled in about:config, regexp pattern modifiers work as expected in the current Firefox Nightly.
N_terminal.label: terminal feature working in Nightly

solution.intent: Implement the requested SpiderMonkey integration by adding a preference wired to the existing irregexp option, updating the test262 feature-check configuration, and re-importing the tests.
solution.concrete_example: Add `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` following the linked preference patch pattern, connect it to the existing JIT option, move `regexp-modifiers` to `FEATURE_CHECK_NEEDED`, run `js/src/tests/test262-update.py`, and build and run the SpiderMonkey tests.

edges.comment: Opening report and c0-c1: the reporter specified the integration work, and participant1 authored separate preference and test patches. The contributor is folded into the simulated user side.

question_patterns: After rebasing and importing the tests, what do the local test run and CI report?
Can you run the SpiderMonkey tests locally and share the raw result from the automation jobs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After rebasing, the tests pass locally for me. The autoland SpiderMonkey jobs do not: they report unexpected failures in regexp-modifier test262 files, including `add-ignoreCase-affects-slash-upper-b.js`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The tests pass both locally and in all of the automation jobs.
The same regexp-modifier tests fail in CI, but I ran them locally through an individual test command rather than the full suite.

edges.comment: c4-c12: participant1 and the reporter both observed local passes, while autoland reported failures. This is a test measurement, so the edge records raw outcomes rather than a conclusion about their cause.

solution.intent: Work around the failures by adding the currently failing regexp-modifier tests to `jstests.list` and landing the remaining subset.
solution.concrete_example: Add the failing dotAll and nested-modifier test262 files to the skip list, confirm the remaining tests pass locally, and reland the preference and test patches.

edges.comment: c7-c10: participant1 rebased the test patch and added the listed failures to the skip list, but the combined landing exposed more CI failures and was backed out. This was a real attempted workaround, not the accepted resolution.

question_patterns: What exact exception and source pattern appear in the CI failure log?
Can you paste the relevant failure lines from one of the failing automation tests?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The log says `SyntaxError: repeated flag in regexp modifier`. One failure points to `add-multiline-does-not-affect-dotAll-flag.js` at the pattern `(?m:es.$)`, with return code 3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is an assertion that the preference is absent and the test harness never attempts to parse a regexp-modifier pattern.
The same syntax error occurs in a different regexp-modifier test file and points to another valid pattern using a repeated outer flag.

edges.comment: c13: the reporter pasted the exact automation exception, file, source pattern, and return code. The conclusion that this proves the feature is enabled belongs to the consuming solution, not to this measurement answer.

solution.intent: Separate the working preference integration from the unresolved test behavior: land the preference patch alone and investigate the repeated-flag failures in the dedicated follow-up instead of continuing to curate a passing test subset.
solution.concrete_example: Land the preference patch after its clean try run, leave the test-enabling patch out for now, and follow the repeated-flag parser failures in the existing dedicated bug rather than adding each newly failing test to `jstests.list`.
solution.inference_hint: The raw CI output shows that regexp-modifier syntax reached the parser. The reporter concluded that the feature check was working and that a separate repeated-flag behavior, shared with the dedicated follow-up bug, was the remaining problem.

edges.comment: c13-c20: after the combined landing was backed out, the reporter landed the clean preference patch alone and explicitly rejected continued skip-list curation in favor of fixing the underlying repeated-flag problem separately.

solution.intent: Complete the experimental feature path by resolving the underlying repeated-flag behavior in its follow-up, retaining the landed preference, and asking an affected user to verify valid regexp modifiers in a current Nightly with the preference enabled.
solution.concrete_example: Keep the experimental `javascript.options.experimental.regexp_modifiers` preference, address the valid-pattern failures in the dedicated follow-up, then ask the user to enable the preference in about:config and retest representative modifier patterns in today's Nightly.

edges.comment: c21-c29: later affected users are folded into the simulated user side. They reproduced the disabled-pref and repeated-flag states, explained how to enable the preference through about:config, and one affected user subsequently confirmed that the feature worked as expected in a current Nightly. The thread does not describe the follow-up patch's internal mechanism, so the solution remains at that stated level.

satisfaction_conditions: Must implement the requested integration around the existing upstream irregexp support: a SpiderMonkey preference controls the feature and the test262 import uses the feature-check path.

Must diagnose the automation failure from the collected evidence: the feature check is enabling regexp modifiers, but valid patterns encounter the separate `repeated flag in regexp modifier` syntax error.
Must not present adding each failing test to `jstests.list` as the final solution; that approach was attempted, additional CI failures remained, and the landing was backed out.
Must separate the clean preference landing from the underlying repeated-flag follow-up rather than repeatedly rebasing both as one blocked landing.
Must ask an affected user to verify representative regexp-modifier patterns in a current build with the experimental preference enabled before declaring the feature working.

persona_hint.experience_level: SpiderMonkey maintainer coordinating a good-first-bug with a new contributor; comfortable with Mercurial, try and autoland jobs, test262 imports, preferences, and reading parser failure logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Friendly, patient, and technically precise; provides concrete commands and failure excerpts, distinguishes local results from CI, and redirects unexpected engine behavior to an appropriate follow-up.
